title: Ten years into Trump’s trade experiment, the US continues to defy expectations
gist: Ten years into the US turn to protectionism, the data contradict the 'bicycle theory' and predictions of calamity: global trade rose to 68% of GDP, US GDP per capita grew fastest in the G7, and the author argues this will entrench nationalist trade policy and pressure others to follow.

insights.claim: Global trade as a share of world GDP rose from 54% in 2016 to 68% in 2025 despite the US turn to economic nationalism, contradicting the 'bicycle theory' that trade collapses without continual liberalisation.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Global trade volume is resilient to US protectionism — don't extrapolate US tariffs into a global trade collapse.
insights.locator: Yet data from the past decade

insights.claim: US real median household income rose from $77,230 in 2016 to $87,460 in 2025 (2025 dollars), and the S&P 500 more than tripled from 2,271.31 on January 20, 2017 to 7,718.60 on September 4, 2026.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Author uses asset and income data to argue tariffs did not produce a Smoot-Hawley-style depression.
insights.quote: But the Trump administration’s trade measures have not produced a new Great Depression.

insights.claim: US GDP per capita grew 18.3% between 2016 and 2025 in constant 2015 dollars, the fastest in the G7.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: The EU-27's GDP fell from 74.4% of US GDP in 2016 to 69% in 2025.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: The IMF projects the US will be the fastest-growing G7 economy in both 2026 and 2027.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Consensus forecasts still favour US growth leadership near term.

insights.claim: Strong data will likely reinforce the Trump administration's view that its trade policies are succeeding and that critics overestimated the risks, making the nationalist approach more durable.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Expect tariffs to persist rather than reverse; plan for structurally higher US trade barriers.

insights.claim: If the US keeps outperforming, other Western countries could face growing pressure to reconsider their own trade strategies; the EU is already belatedly following Washington in erecting barriers to Chinese exports, per Michael Froman.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Rising EU trade barriers against China — negative for Chinese exporters to Europe, supportive for EU domestic producers.

insights.claim: As US policymakers treat trade policy like tax policy — set on a national basis — the debate may shift from what can be done to what should be done, echoing the repeated US trade-policy reversals over 250 years.
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
insights.so_what: Trade policy becomes a routine domestic lever, raising policy volatility across administrations.
